How does a *rate of change* differ from an ordinary *rate*? What do you need to measure each?

```{devoirs_choices}
#| label: choices_nep.1.udls
- 'A rate needs one snapshot; a rate of change needs one snapshot too, but with different units.':
    correct: false
    feedback: 'Sorry. If you are going to look at how something changes, you need a before-and-after measurement.'
- 'A rate is one quantity divided by another from a single snapshot; a rate of change uses *changes* in two quantities (numerator and denominator), so you need at least two "frames" (e.g., a short "movie") to form the ratio of those changes.':
    correct: true
- 'A rate of change is always with respect to time; an ordinary rate is not.':
    correct: false
    feedback: 'No. The rate of change can be with respect to any quantity, for instance the rate of change of student test scores with respect to parental education.'
- 'There is no real difference; the terms are interchangeable.':
    correct: false
    feedback: 'While it''s true that a rate of change is also a rate, not every rate is a rate of change.'
```
